versions.notes: United Arab Emirates. Accession effective 1983-12-15.  The US Coast Guard's international pages supply the selected text. IMO A.464(XII) added Rule 22(d) on 1 June 1983. The UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency's amendment table identifies subsequent changes elsewhere in the Rules.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Length overall and greatest breadth
sections.text: (j) The words length and breadth of a vessel mean her length overall and greatest breadth.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 3 introduces definitions except where the context otherwise requires.

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5 Look-out Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Applies at all times. Rule 4 covers any condition of visibility.

Rule 22. VISIBILITY OF LIGHTS The lights prescribed in these Rules shall have an intensity as specified in Section 8 of Annex I to these Regulations so as to be visible at the following minimum ranges:

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Length overall and greatest breadth
sections.text: (j) The words "length" and "breadth" of a vessel mean her length overall and greatest breadth.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 3 introduces definitions except where the context otherwise requires.

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5. LOOK-OUT Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Applies at all times. Rule 4 covers any condition of visibility.

sections.title: Minimum visibility ranges of prescribed lights
sections.caveat: Complete comparison text for Rule 22. Individual lettered paragraphs are screened by vessel particulars.

sections.title: Light ranges at 50 metres overall and above
sections.text:
Rule 22. VISIBILITY OF LIGHTS The lights prescribed in these Rules shall have an intensity as specified in Section 8 of Annex I to these Regulations so as to be visible at the following minimum ranges:
(a) in vessels of 50 metres or more in length: a masthead light, 6 miles; a sidelight, 3 miles; a sternlight, 3 miles; a towing light, 3 miles; a white, red, green or yellow all-round light, 3 miles;

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 22 sets ranges for lights prescribed elsewhere. Check the vessel's required light arrangement, Rule 1(e) determinations and any historical Rule 38(a) relief. Rule 3(j) uses length overall.

sections.title: Light ranges from 12 to under 50 metres overall
sections.text: (b) in vessels of 12 metres or more in length but less than 50 metres in length: a masthead light, 5 miles; except than where the length of the vessel is less than 20 metres, 3 miles; a sidelight, 2 miles; a sternlight, 2 miles; a towing light, 2 miles; a white, red, green or yellow all-round light, 2 miles;

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 22 sets ranges for lights prescribed elsewhere. Check the vessel's required light arrangement, Rule 1(e) determinations and any historical Rule 38(a) relief. Rule 3(j) uses length overall. Paragraph (b) gives a shorter masthead-light range below 20 metres.

sections.text: (c) in vessels of less than 12 metres in length: a masthead light, 2 miles; a sidelight, 1 mile; a sternlight, 2 miles; a towing light, 2 miles; a white, red, green or yellow all-round light, 2 miles.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5. LOOK-OUT Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Length overall and greatest breadth
sections.text: (j) The words "length" and "breadth" of a vessel mean her length overall and greatest breadth.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 3 introduces definitions except where the context otherwise requires.

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5. LOOK-OUT Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Applies at all times. Rule 4 covers any condition of visibility.

sections.caveat: Complete comparison text for Rule 22. Individual lettered paragraphs are screened by vessel particulars.

sections.title: Light ranges at 50 metres overall and above
sections.text:
Rule 22. VISIBILITY OF LIGHTS The lights prescribed in these Rules shall have an intensity as specified in Section 8 of Annex I to these Regulations so as to be visible at the following minimum ranges:
(a) in vessels of 50 metres or more in length: a masthead light, 6 miles; a sidelight, 3 miles; a sternlight, 3 miles; a towing light, 3 miles; a white, red, green or yellow all-round light, 3 miles;

sections.caveat: Rule 22 sets ranges for lights prescribed elsewhere. Check the vessel's required light arrangement, Rule 1(e) determinations and any historical Rule 38(a) relief. Rule 3(j) uses length overall.

(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.

sections.text:

(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.text: Rule 5. LOOK-OUT Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Length overall and greatest breadth
sections.text: (j) The words length and breadth of a vessel mean her length overall and greatest breadth.

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5 Look-out Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

sections.caveat: Applies at all times. Rule 4 covers any condition of visibility.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:

(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Length overall and greatest breadth
sections.text: (j) The words length and breadth of a vessel mean her length overall and greatest breadth.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5 Look-out Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Applies at all times. Rule 4 covers any condition of visibility.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1 Application
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbors, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2 Responsibility
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

versions.notes: South Africa. Accession effective 1977-07-15.  Concluded on 20 October 1972 and registered with the UN on 8 August 1977. The 1977 Treaty Series reproduces the original Regulations and their recorded rectifications.

sections.title: Waters covered and local special rules
sections.text:
Rule 1. APPLICATION
(a) These Rules shall apply to all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
(b) Nothing in these Rules shall interfere with the operation of special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected with the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels. Such special rules shall conform as closely as possible to these Rules.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Rule 1(b) preserves local special rules. Check the competent authority's demarcation and local rules for the waters where the boat operates.

sections.title: Responsibility of the vessel, owner, master and crew
sections.text:
Rule 2. RESPONSIBILITY
(a) Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or of the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case.
(b) In construing and complying with these Rules due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and collision and to any special circumstances, including the limitations of the vessels involved, which may make a departure from these Rules necessary to avoid immediate danger.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: The rule addresses vessels, owners, masters and crew. Paragraph (b) covers special circumstances and immediate danger.

sections.title: Length overall and greatest breadth

sections.title: Look-out
sections.text: Rule 5. LOOK-OUT Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

all.source: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, COLREG 1972, party or territorial record

sections.caveat: Applies at all times. Rule 4 covers any condition of visibility.

sections.text:
Rule 22. VISIBILITY OF LIGHTS The lights prescribed in these Rules shall have an intensity as specified in Section 8 of Annex I to these Regulations so as to be visible at the following minimum ranges:
(a) in vessels of 50 metres or more in length: a masthead light, 6 miles; a sidelight, 3 miles; a sternlight, 3 miles; a towing light, 3 miles; a white, red, green or yellow all-round light, 3 miles;

coverage: Named parties and selected explicitly dated territorial applications. The IMO register also records declarations, reservations, former territories and disputed extensions on pages 110–116. Coastal-state and local navigation law can govern vessels under other flags. The indexed text is limited to the specified international rules.
